newsitem.title: USA: NYS jobless rate rises to 6.9 pct, NYC's leaps too.
newsitem.headline: NYS jobless rate rises to 6.9 pct, NYC's leaps too.

text.p: New York State Department of Labor said the state's unemployment rate rose one percentage point to 6.9 percent in January, while New York City's rate shot up 1.1 percentage points to 9.9 percent.

The state shrugged off the increases, saying they were not severe and mainly were due to stores and service providers reducing staffs after the holiday season, as well as semester breaks at schools and colleges, and the winter's curbing work outside work.

"This January's decline in jobs was better than average for this time of year and the rise in unemployment was typical for January. New York's economy remains healthy," said Thomas Rodick, director of the state labor department's Division of Research and Statistics, in prepared remarks, on Wednesday.

When measured against the year-ago level, the state's unemployment rate was unchanged at 6.9 percent, though that was not the case for New York City, whose January, 1997, rate was one full percentage point above the 8.9 reading seen a year-ago.

New York City Deputy Mayor for Operations, Randy Mastro, noting in a Reuters interview that recent reports showed the city's jobless rate rate stood at 8.6 percent, added that this marked a 20 percent decline in this gauge since Mayor Rudolph Guiliani took office in 1994.

Mastro also told the New York Times that having a higher number of job seekers was in itself a measure of growing strength. "It's a reflection of an improving local economy that not only private-sector jobs increased, but more people want to enter the job market," he was quoted as saying, in the paper's Thursday edition.
